title: Parashurama Avatar: The Sage Who Carried an Axe
sources: Bhagavata Purana, Canto 9, chapters 15-16 (Jamadagni, Kartavirya Arjuna and the theft of Kamadhenu, the king's defeat, the revenge of his sons, the twenty-one campaigns, the gift of the earth, Mount Mahendra)
Mahabharata, Vana Parva and Shanti Parva (Parashurama and the Kshatriyas); later tradition for Shiva's gift of the axe and the land reclaimed from the sea on the western coast

lines.text: Long ago, a boy was born to the sage Jamadagni,
lines.caps: LONG *AGO | A *BOY | WAS *BORN | TO THE SAGE | *JAMADAGNI
lines.say: Long ago, a boy was born to the sage Jumma-dugnee,

lines.text: with the calm of a priest, and the fire of a warrior.
lines.caps: THE *CALM | OF A *PRIEST | AND THE *FIRE | OF A *WARRIOR

lines.text: He prayed to Shiva for years, and Shiva gave him a blazing axe.
lines.caps: HE *PRAYED | TO *SHIVA | FOR *YEARS | AND SHIVA | *GAVE HIM | A *BLAZING AXE

lines.text: From that day, he was called Parashurama, Rama with the axe.
lines.caps: FROM THAT *DAY | HE WAS *CALLED | *PARASHURAMA | *RAMA | WITH THE *AXE
lines.say: From that day, he was called Puh-rushoo-rahma, Rahma with the axe.

lines.text: In those days, a king with a thousand arms ruled without mercy.
lines.caps: IN THOSE *DAYS | A *KING | WITH A *THOUSAND ARMS | RULED | WITHOUT *MERCY

lines.text: One day he visited the sage's quiet home, and saw their wish granting cow.
lines.caps: ONE *DAY | HE *VISITED | THE SAGE'S | *QUIET HOME | AND *SAW | THEIR *WISH GRANTING | *COW

lines.text: She could conjure a feast for a whole army, out of thin air.
lines.caps: SHE COULD *CONJURE | A *FEAST | FOR A WHOLE *ARMY | OUT OF *THIN AIR

lines.text: He wanted her, so he simply took her by force.
lines.caps: HE *WANTED HER | SO HE *SIMPLY | *TOOK HER | BY *FORCE

lines.text: When Parashurama returned, he stormed the palace alone,
lines.caps: WHEN *PARASHURAMA | *RETURNED | HE *STORMED | THE *PALACE | *ALONE
lines.say: When Puh-rushoo-rahma returned, he stormed the palace alone,

lines.text: defeated the thousand armed king, and brought the cow home.
lines.caps: *DEFEATED | THE THOUSAND ARMED *KING | AND *BROUGHT | THE COW *HOME

lines.text: But the king's sons took a cruel revenge, and his father was lost.
lines.caps: BUT THE KING'S *SONS | TOOK A *CRUEL | *REVENGE | AND HIS *FATHER | WAS *LOST

lines.text: Heartbroken, Parashurama made a vow, to free the earth from every tyrant.
lines.caps: *HEARTBROKEN | PARASHURAMA | MADE A *VOW | TO *FREE | THE *EARTH | FROM EVERY *TYRANT
lines.say: Heartbroken, Puh-rushoo-rahma made a vow, to free the earth from every tyrant.

lines.text: Twenty one times he crossed the land, and no cruel king could stand before his axe.
lines.caps: *TWENTY ONE TIMES | HE *CROSSED | THE *LAND | AND NO *CRUEL KING | COULD *STAND | BEFORE HIS *AXE

lines.text: His anger burned like a forest fire.
lines.caps: HIS *ANGER | *BURNED | LIKE A *FOREST FIRE

lines.text: But when it was over, he laid his anger down, and gave away everything he had won,
lines.caps: BUT WHEN IT WAS *OVER | HE *LAID | HIS *ANGER DOWN | AND *GAVE AWAY | *EVERYTHING | HE HAD *WON

lines.text: and cast his axe into the sea, where the waters drew back, and new land rose.
lines.caps: AND *CAST | HIS *AXE | INTO THE *SEA | WHERE THE *WATERS | DREW *BACK | AND NEW *LAND | *ROSE

lines.text: Then he climbed a mountain to meditate, where it is said he lives to this day,
lines.caps: THEN HE *CLIMBED | A *MOUNTAIN | TO *MEDITATE | WHERE IT IS *SAID | HE *LIVES | TO THIS *DAY

lines.text: waiting to teach the heroes yet to come.
lines.caps: *WAITING | TO *TEACH | THE *HEROES | YET TO *COME

lines.text: This is Parashurama, the sixth avatar of Vishnu,
lines.caps: THIS IS *PARASHURAMA | THE *SIXTH | *AVATAR | OF *VISHNU
lines.say: This is Puh-rushoo-rahma, the sixth avatar of Vishnu,

lines.text: a reminder that true strength protects the weak, and knows when to lay its weapon down.
lines.caps: A *REMINDER | TRUE *STRENGTH | *PROTECTS | THE *WEAK | AND *KNOWS | WHEN TO *LAY | ITS *WEAPON | *DOWN
